_comment: Per-section assessments for CURRENT_STATE_AUDIT.md. The SECTION LIST is not
here — it is read out of the specification at generation time so a section
cannot be omitted. This file only says what is known about each one.
A section absent from this file is printed as NOT_ASSESSED. That is
deliberate: NOT_STARTED would assert that no work exists, which is a claim
nobody has earned for a section they have not read. Most NOT_ASSESSED
sections here are probably done — §84 evidence covers a lot of ground — but
Statuses must come from §0.1's vocabulary; the generator rejects anything
else. NOT_APPLICABLE requires justification in the evidence field.

9.evidence: Checked against §9's own text rather than assumed. Metadata split is correct — the database holds provenance, hashes and versions while object storage holds the files, and no PDF is in a BLOB column. Version preservation was NOT met and is now: B-27 found that the UNIQUE index on (country_code, program, form_code) forced a new revision to overwrite its predecessor's row, orphaning the previous PDF in storage with nothing pointing at it. `form_template_versions` (migration 20260824400000) fixes it, applied to both databases — 66 versions, 66 active, 0 unversioned.
9.remaining: §9's recommended metadata list is not fully covered: authority, original filename, MIME type, language, publication/effective dates and copyright/redistribution metadata have no columns. None is load-bearing today — every cached form is a PDF fetched from a registered official source — but they should be recorded as a deliberate omission rather than an unnoticed one.

18.evidence: §18's hard requirement is met by construction, and checked rather than assumed: there is NO OpenAI server-side conversation state anywhere in the codebase — no previous_response_id, no conversation_id against OpenAI (every conversation_id match is VisaAI's own messaging tables). So OpenAI state cannot be the source of truth for visa requirements or application records, because it does not exist. Application state lives in Postgres; LangGraph checkpoints live in Upstash Redis with an explicit 7-day expiry (`{ ex: 86400 * 7 }` in checkpoint.service.ts), so context is not retained indefinitely. Compaction exists where it was measured to matter: voice windows to 8 turns, messaging to 20.
18.remaining: The intake question node sends the full transcript every turn against a ~2,700-token system prompt — no windowing at all. Already recorded as D-06 and deliberately deferred: changing what the model sees needs the eval suite first, and no eval has run against a funded key (BL-1).

42.evidence: Implemented against §42's conditions rather than as a convention copied from elsewhere. Generated from the registry at request time (the binding condition is 'automatically maintained' — a hand-written manifest goes stale, which is this codebase's recurring failure); lists only what visa_publishable_pages already exposes, so no private data; replaces nothing; and states in its OWN header that it is experimental, not a standard, and not a ranking mechanism. Verified live: HTTP 200, text/plain, 13 destinations and 58 routes, exactly matching the registry. The proxy matcher would have 307'd it into the localised app — the robots.txt bug — so llms.txt is excluded and a test now reads the pattern out of proxy.ts and asserts it, proved by deleting the exclusion and watching it fail.

48.evidence: Checked against the live page rather than the architecture doc, which is what turned this from assumed-fine into a finding. A visa detail page carried exactly TWO internal /visas links — /visas and /visas/canada, both breadcrumb up-links — so every detail page was a leaf and a country's routes were connected to each other only through the hub. Detail pages now render 'Other {country} visas' linking every sibling route, which matters more here than the usual related-content filler because choosing between routes IS the applicant's actual problem: most arrive knowing where they want to go and not which visa that needs.

68.evidence: Measured on production rather than assumed. `visa_publishable_pages` — the read path behind every public page — plans and executes in 7.1ms; its sequential scans are correct at 196 countries / 79 types / 1,023 requirements, where an index would be slower. No N+1 on the public path: the country hub issues one Promise.all of two queries and nothing per visa type. No large payloads: every read of visa_source_versions names its columns, so the normalized_text column added for B-29 cannot leak into a hot path. Registry-ops endpoint costs: counts 0.8-9.5ms, active-source scan 0.5ms.
68.remaining: Connection pooling under load is untested and untestable here — BL-4, no staging environment, and load-testing production is not on the table. One known bound recorded in code: the staleness computation fetches every active source into JS; 0.5ms at 235 sources, to be moved into SQL if the count reaches the low thousands.

71.evidence: Not just present — watching, and proved end to end in production. The engine was live and ticking every 5 minutes with ZERO rules and ZERO events ever fired, because nothing described whether the source data was sound. `RegistryMetricsService` (key `registry`) adds it, and four rules run against it: provenance defects > 0, parse errors > 2, published pages < 50, review queue > 150. Verified live 2026-08-24: all four evaluate on schedule — pages 58 ok, provenance 0 ok, queue 125 ok, parse errors breached at 9 then recovered to 0 after a fix. Verifying it also found B-30, where an unevaluable rule fired a false RECOVERY.
71.remaining: Thresholds are judgement and only one has been tested against reality so far. Notification recipients are empty — a breach records an event and logs, but nobody is paged yet; that needs a decision about who.

74.evidence: Both halves verified, and they are different questions. ACCESS, checked against production: GET /admin/registry-ops returns 401 unauthenticated, /registry 307s to /login, and the anonymous response carries no registry data. RENDERING, which a 401 says nothing about: 5 tests render the assembled page and assert what an authorised admin actually sees — an unattributable change shows as 'Unknown — previous text not retained' with no fabricated +/- counts, a real change shows its reasons and counts, a failed load says the figures are unknown rather than printing zeros, and a missing run reports itself rather than rendering an empty one.
